audit_findings.title: Parent-share numerator may be mixed with consolidated-basis adjustments
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 consolidated net income was $55.995m, including $23.358m attributable to NCI, versus $32.637m attributable to Universal; the OE correction is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE numerator may combine parent-attributable income with consolidated depreciation, maintenance capex, and other adjustments, while per-share value is assigned only to parent common shares; consolidated cash and capital requirements may also include NCI claims.
audit_findings.evidence: The net income and shareholders’ equity attributable to the noncontrolling interests in these subsidiaries are reported in the consolidated financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The economic-perimeter mismatch is demonstrated if the stated consolidated cash-flow add-backs were applied to parent-attributable earnings. The $23.358m NCI income component equals 34.4% of the $68m anchor, so an allocation error is reasonably capable of changing value. Direction cannot be established without knowing the NCI share of each add-back, maintenance-capex deduction, and bridge asset.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild all OE years on one perimeter: either allocate income, D&A, maintenance capex, working capital, cash, and other bridge items to Universal shareholders, or calculate consolidated OE and deduct the complete NCI claim; rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may be seasonal operating liquidity rather than excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $173.593m, or $6.78 per diluted share; June total debt was $1,183.880m and net debt was $1,013.818m
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation adds the entire June cash balance to the equity bridge even though the cash may fund seasonal inventory and may be financed by short-term borrowings or partly attributable to NCI.
audit_findings.evidence: We also periodically may have large cash balances that we utilize to meet our working capital requirements.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that cash and borrowings finance seasonal crop purchases, but it does not establish how much June cash is distributable surplus. Removing the full add-back would reduce each scenario by $6.78 per share, lowering base value from $42.11 to $35.33 and bull value from $46.24 to $39.46. The actual correction may be smaller, but the open exposure is clearly material.
audit_findings.action: Measure minimum cash across the full crop cycle, reconcile the June cash increase to borrowings and working-capital movements, identify restricted or subsidiary/NCI cash, and rerun the bridge using only parent-accessible surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: Scenario growth may not fund the capital required to produce it
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2027 planned capex is $55m-$65m versus typical maintenance capex below $30m; using the supplied 3.3% RONTA, first-year 2%-4% growth on $68m OE implies $41.2m-$82.4m of incremental capital, computed
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth increases forecast OE without an explicit deduction for incremental fixed assets, inventory, supplier advances, receivables, or associated financing costs.
audit_findings.evidence: We currently plan to spend approximately $55 to $65 million in fiscal year 2027 on capital projects for maintenance of our facilities and other investments to grow and improve our businesses.
audit_findings.explanation: The growth-capital omission is a demonstrated modeling risk, although the exact correction is unresolved because maintenance and growth capex are not separated. The computed capital requirement is large relative to the $68m anchor and excludes additional working-capital needs, making the 2%-4% scenarios reasonably capable of overstating value materially.
audit_findings.action: Separate maintenance from growth capex, forecast incremental working capital and financing costs for each growth rate, deduct those investments before distributable OE, and rerun every scenario including terminal value.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method affiliates create a maintenance-capex blind spot
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 affiliate amounts were $3.430m pretax earnings, $1.612m after-tax earnings, and $1.857m dividends; omitted maintenance capex, working capital, and net debt are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent earnings include equity-method income, while consolidated D&A, capex, working capital, and debt exclude the affiliates' corresponding amounts, potentially overstating OE attributed to the affiliate interest.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s 49% ownership interest in Socotab L.L.C. (“Socotab”), a leading supplier of oriental tobaccos with operations located principally in Eastern Europe and Türkiye, is the primary investment accounted for under the equity method.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter asymmetry is demonstrated, but the record does not disclose Socotab's maintenance investment, leverage, capital calls, or sustainable distributions. The latest after-tax earnings contribution is only 2.4% of the $68m anchor and dividends exceeded that year's earnings, but those figures cannot bound undisclosed affiliate capital and financial claims; materiality therefore remains uncertain.
audit_findings.action: Obtain affiliate financial statements and distribution history, replace equity income with sustainable parent cash distributions or incorporate Universal's proportional maintenance capex, working capital, taxes, and net financial claims, then rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Routine inventory losses must not be normalized away
audit_findings.magnitude: $51.988m FY2026 inventory write-down, equal to 76.5% of the $68m OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back or excluding the write-down as a noncash or unusual item would raise anchor and trend OE even though recurring inventory losses are an operating cost.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that write-downs are routine and reports $52.0m, $19.8m, and $9.2m for fiscal 2026, 2025, and 2024. The supplied record does not show the OE reconciliation, so reversal of the charge is an unresolved possibility rather than a demonstrated valuation error. If reversed, its size is plainly capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Produce the year-by-year OE reconciliation, verify that inventory write-downs and related inventory cash-flow effects were not added back or normalized away, and rerun anchor, trend, and scenarios if any reversal occurred.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retirement claims may require a cash-basis adjustment
audit_findings.magnitude: $35.3m combined unfunded PBO, or $1.38 per diluted share; FY2026 employer contributions were $13.758m versus $2.277m net periodic benefit cost
audit_findings.mechanism: OE contains accounting pension expense, while actual contributions and pay-as-you-go benefits may differ; alternatively, the unfunded obligation may require an equity-bridge deduction if its future cash costs are not captured in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The unfunded PBO for those pension plans and postretirement benefit plans was $ 21.1 million and $ 14.2 million, respectively, at March 31, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligations and recent accounting-to-cash difference are demonstrated, but neither the normalized future cash shortfall nor the amount already reflected in OE is established. A full $35.3m bridge deduction would equal 3.3% of base equity value and would reduce bull value from $46.24 to about $44.86 per share, but applying both a cash-cost adjustment and a liability deduction could double count the claim.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile plan-specific GAAP expense to normalized contributions and pay-as-you-go benefits, project the unfunded plans' cash payments, choose either a cash-basis OE adjustment or a residual bridge deduction without double counting, and rerun the scenarios.
